title: Jacobson density
source: Bezrukavnikov, MIT 18.706, Theorem 3.3 (field setting); Algebra Core, Simple and semisimple modules
proof_check: Use the opposite endomorphism ring for the right action and separate a proper cyclic submodule of the finite direct sum.

title: Density in the finite topology and the finite-dimensional quotient
source: Bezrukavnikov, MIT 18.706, Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.5; finite-topology formulation in this supplement
proof_check: Interpolate on a basis of the span of the finite test set; a full finite basis gives surjectivity.

title: A proper dense image
source: Finite-rank operator example developed in this supplement; density theorem in Bezrukavnikov, MIT 18.706
proof_check: Matrix units compute the commutant; a unilateral shift has infinite rank after subtraction of any scalar.

title: Central simple algebras
source: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0753; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/074Y
proof_check: Conventions preserve finite dimension, a nonzero unit, and centrality over the given field.

title: Matrix and division presentations
source: P1-03 Algebra Core ALG-03-C03-R04 (v0.22.0, provenance/components/AlgebraCore/delivery/paper.tex:708); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0753
proof_check: The division-factor comparison uses the opposite of the endomorphism ring as a k-algebra.

title: The enveloping algebra of a central simple algebra
source: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/074I; P1-03 Algebra Core ALG-03-C03-R04
proof_check: The regular bimodule is simple and its commuting endomorphisms are precisely the k-scalars; equal dimensions give injectivity.

title: Tensor product and base change
source: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0748, Lemmas 11.4.1 and 11.4.7–11.4.9
proof_check: The first tensor factor supplies every k-linear coefficient extraction, and only the second factor must be simple.

title: Degree and finite Galois splitting
source: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0752; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0753; D07 K07.23.finite_division_ring and K07.23.algebraically_closed_center (v0.22.0, docs/notes-revisions/v0.13.0/D07/chapters/M07.23.tex:40,78)
proof_check: The generic discriminant argument applies to arbitrary infinite base fields, and comparison of minimal polynomials requires only linear independence after extending scalars.

title: Index and degrees of splitting extensions
source: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0751; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0752
proof_check: Restriction of the split column representation gives the divisibility; a division factor may be used once uniqueness is checked after base change.

title: Skolem–Noether
source: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/074P, Theorem 11.6.1
proof_check: The two actions on the left regular module both use the opposite of B and need B simple with arbitrary center.

title: Centralizer and double centralizer
source: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/074T; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/074S, Lemma 11.7.2
proof_check: The endomorphism algebra of the bimodule is the opposite of the centralizer; dimension and inclusion yield the double centralizer.

title: Maximal subfields of a central division algebra
source: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/074S, Lemmas 11.7.3–11.7.4; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/074X, Lemma 11.8.3
proof_check: Maximality implies self-centralization, which gives degree and splitting even for a possibly inseparable maximal field.

title: Reduced characteristic polynomial
source: Linear Algebraic Groups, F05 (unpublished notes); N. Elkies, Reduced norm in a central simple algebra, https://abel.math.harvard.edu/~elkies/M250.04/reduced.html
proof_check: The coefficientwise argument uses a generic element, so it also proves descent of the polynomial over finite fields.

title: Brauer equivalence and the group law
source: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/074J
proof_check: Equality of division factors identifies the equivalence relation; the opposite product is split via the enveloping map.

title: The real and quaternion classes
source: D07 K07.23.quaternion_algebra and K07.23.frobenius (v0.22.0, docs/notes-revisions/v0.13.0/D07/chapters/M07.23.tex:99,129); N. Elkies, https://abel.math.harvard.edu/~elkies/M250.04/reduced.html
proof_dependencies: RM03-C04.02 | RM03-C04.04 | RM03-C04.09 | RM03-C04.10 | RM03-C04.11 | D07:K07.23.frobenius | D07:K07.23.quaternion_algebra
proof_check: Frobenius exhausts division representatives; the explicit complex matrices yield the quaternion norm.

title: Relative classes and descent
source: Stacks Project, §59.61, Equation (59.61.5.1) and Theorem 59.61.6; Colliot-Thélène and Skorobogatov, The Brauer–Grothendieck Group, Theorem 1.3.5. These locate the result and sign convention.
proof_check: Semilinear vector descent proves the fixed-degree classification. The scalar regular representation proves surjectivity and scalar correction proves injectivity. Continuous cochains reduce to finite Galois layers. The cocycle is the inverse of the Stacks convention with the same lifts.

title: Morita equivalence from a full idempotent
source: Algebra Core, Morita equivalence from a progenerator; Bezrukavnikov, MIT 18.706, Proposition 7.7 (left-module convention)
proof_check: Evaluation at e identifies the dual bimodule with Re; balanced multiplication identifies M tensor Re with Me.

title: A matrix corner and a non-full corner
source: Algebra Core, matrix ring example following the progenerator theorem; Algebraic K-Theory, A10; product-ring example developed here
proof_check: The matrix-unit expression gives fullness; the product-ring corner kills the other summand.

title: Algebra representations and modules
source: Crawley-Boevey, Representations of Algebras (2025), Section 1.1, PDF p. 3; Algebra Core, Ch. 1 and the group-algebra specialization in Ch. 8
proof_check: On a fixed vector space, the two unital action descriptions and their maps agree.

title: Quivers and path algebras
source: Crawley-Boevey, Representations of Algebras (2025), Section 1.3, PDF pp. 12–14
proof_check: Finite vertex and arrow sets, including the allowed case of oriented cycles.

title: Multiplication and the path basis
source: Crawley-Boevey, Representations of Algebras (2025), Section 1.3, PDF pp. 13–15
proof_check: Associativity with zero for noncomposable paths; finite dimension exactly for an acyclic finite quiver.

title: Quiver representations
source: Crawley-Boevey, Representations of Algebras (2025), Section 1.3, PDF pp. 12–13
proof_check: Arrow maps go from source to target.

title: Quiver representations and path algebra modules
source: Crawley-Boevey, Representations of Algebras (2025), Section 1.3, PDF pp. 14–16
proof_check: Two inverse constructions on objects and morphisms; vertexwise kernels and cokernels prove exactness.

title: Relations and admissible ideals
source: Crawley-Boevey, Representations of Algebras (2025), Section 1.4, PDF pp. 16–17
proof_check: Relations are linear combinations of parallel paths; the arrow ideal defines admissibility.

title: The module category with relations
source: Crawley-Boevey, Representations of Algebras (2025), Sections 1.3–1.4, PDF pp. 14–17
proof_check: The relation generators act by zero if and only if their two-sided ideal acts by zero.

title: Finiteness from admissibility
source: Crawley-Boevey, Representations of Algebras (2025), Section 1.4, PDF pp. 16–17
proof_check: Arrow-ideal powers consist of the longer paths; vertex and arrow images have no relations of degree below two.

title: One arrow and a triangular matrix algebra
source: Crawley-Boevey, Representations of Algebras (2025), Section 1.3, PDF p. 14
proof_check: The arrow maps to the lower-triangular matrix unit E21 under the fixed left-module convention.

title: One loop with a square-zero relation
source: Crawley-Boevey, Representations of Algebras (2025), Sections 1.3–1.4, PDF pp. 14, 16–17; square-zero example developed here
proof_check: The one-loop path algebra is a polynomial algebra and the square relation makes the loop operator square zero.
